Revoking Shizuku access force-stops this app. Some systems also disable its accessibility service. After reopening the app, restore the key service in system settings; helper mode also needs it.

Once key detection is restored, helper mode adjusts volume through Android audio APIs. Some phones still restrict background writes. The panel shows actual system volume and the adjustment result.

This app declares standard Android boot permission, granted at installation, and uses boot broadcasts to restore volume monitoring.

Your system also has startup management. Allow this app to auto-start in app settings or the phone manager. Some systems also offer “Associated startup”. Allow background activity in battery settings, using options such as “Unrestricted” or “Allow high background power usage”; names vary by system.

If this app is missing from the auto-start list or app settings, export diagnostics. An abnormal installation record may hide the entry. Reinstalling may recreate the record but clears app settings, so note your step count first. Updating usually preserves the record. The app cannot grant manufacturer startup permissions itself.

This app declares standard Android boot permission, granted at installation, and uses boot broadcasts to restore foreground volume monitoring.\n\nAllow background notifications and disable battery optimization for this app. If your system provides extra auto-start or background activity settings, allow the app there too. The system decides whether an auto-start entry appears in app settings.

Allow Precise Volume to run in the background in system app settings or battery management. Options may be called “Unrestricted”, “Allow background activity”, or “Allow high background power usage”.\n\nThe system background management page will open. If no dedicated page is available, the system settings page for this app will open.

This mode adjusts volume using Shizuku Root or ADB access and monitors volume and power keys directly on dedicated input devices while unlocked, locked, or with the screen off. It automatically restores this app’s accessibility service for the vivo lock-screen panel; key detection and correction remain privileged and do not depend on that service. Touch coordinates and text keys are not read.

Start Shizuku using Root, wireless debugging, or ADB on a computer, then authorize Precise Volume. Some vivo systems intercept screen-off volume keys. A helper that only writes volume cannot handle those keys; Shizuku key monitoring is needed in that case.

System screen-off shortcuts may still react to volume keys. Disable conflicting shortcuts such as screen-off quick launch or quick camera. Screen-off long presses adjust on release using repeat count or duration. Calls remain under system control.

After rebooting, check that Shizuku is running. Services started using wireless debugging or ADB must be started again. If the connection drops, key correction pauses until Shizuku reconnects. The app shows the current connection status.

Install “Precise Volume Helper (separate app)”, included with this app, and allow “Associated startup” in the helper system permission settings. The main app connects automatically while running. Background volume writes need no Root or Shizuku.

Some tested vivo firmware intercepts accessibility keys while locked or with the screen off. Helper 1.4 can read physical volume and power key states on the lit lock screen and while the screen is off. Use the helper screen-off access button to copy the USB ADB command or grant permission once using an already running Shizuku:

adb shell pm grant com.vivo.finevolumesteps.helper android.permission.DUMP

Shizuku only grants this permission and does not switch volume modes automatically. Authorization survives app and phone restarts; reinstalling the helper requires a new grant. Monitoring handles locked and screen-off keys in helper mode and is prepared early for wireless media playback. Without authorization, the accessibility service still handles unlocked screen-on keys. Calls remain under system control.

This helper is independently developed and is not affiliated with vivo. System updates may change compatibility. If it cannot connect, check the helper associated startup permission.
